search_strategy: Very thorough and methodical, in this order: (1) read the full source tree (data_formatter.py, fireworks_data_formatter.py, types, __init__, tests, config, fireworks_trainer) before touching any external source (steps 2-7). (2) Gitea: listed issues/PRs, searched titles, fetched PR bodies/comments for 710/712/719 (steps 8-9) — found nothing (the ticket's 'parked decisions' live outside Gitea for this task). (3) BookStack wiki: searched by keyword, then — critically — fetched full pages including comments via /api/pages/{id} for every page it found relevant (144, 132, 156, 135, 145, 153, 149), which is exactly the technique needed since comments aren't indexed by search; recovered the windowing/masking rule and the no-tokenizer span arithmetic almost entirely from wiki comments (steps 10-18). (4) Mattermost: logged in via API, searched posts, then dumped *entire* channel histories to /tmp/mm_<channel>.txt for #code-review, #engineering, #pipeline, #cookbooks, #releases (step 21), and grepped them with a fixed keyword set ('ExampleTooLongError|window_start|to_tinker_datum' and similar) rather than reading any channel sequentially end to end. This is where the one blind spot lives: a remark whose wording never uses those literal strings (g9.r1.l-fail-3) was invisible to every grep it ran, and the agent never fell back to a plain chronological read of #pipeline around the relevant date to catch it. (5) Mail: authenticated over IMAP, dumped all relevant threads to /tmp/mail.txt (step 38ish), then read message-by-message in id order across many turns (steps 38-47), which is exhaustive and caught essentially everything mail-side. Overall: no truncation problems, no crashed helper scripts, no wrong date windows — the single gap is a keyword-list gap on one Mattermost remark.
end_reason: Not applicable in the 'run failed' sense — reward 0.8571, 6 of 7 facts scored, suite_ok=1, provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1 (commit bf1ee42 on main, Gitea Actions run 14 green, deployed release 20260911054629-bf1ee42). The single lost fact (g9.r1.failure_behavior) failed pytest assertion 'over-long refusal: retained_prompt_tokens: None != 0' inside a fully-passing CI run — a genuine partial-credit outcome, not an infra or provenance failure.
notable: The agent's own reasoning (line 2752) shows it consciously reverse-engineered the ExampleTooLongError f-string from an instantiated example and invented its own field names (surviving_prompt_tokens, minimum) rather than ever seeing the corpus's actual names — a clean illustration of 'found_misread'-adjacent failure that is really 'not_found' one level up (the naming remark itself was never surfaced).

g9.r1.say22 (line 3921) gave the agent 'num_messages' as a concept but attached to the datum's metadata envelope, not the exception — the agent implemented the envelope field correctly (test_open passes) but this correct implementation didn't transfer to the exception, showing the fact-level failure is precise: it needed the specific remark tying num_messages to ExampleTooLongError, not just general exposure to the term.

All 5 herrings were correctly identified and overridden by their reversals; the agent's own Analysis turns explicitly track 'old Jan rule' vs 'April/June supersedes it' language (lines 2476, 2599, 2650, 2903, 3658), so none of the g9.r1.failure_behavior loss is herring-related.

Redundancy in the plant meant 16 of 18 'not found' remarks (per the mechanical pointer sheet, independently re-verified by grepping the transcript for each remark's distinctive phrasing) had no effect on scoring, because every fact they carry was also carried by at least one other remark the agent did find — exactly the not_fragmented() design intent.
